# Research problem and questions

Text-independent speaker verification must distinguish same-speaker from different-speaker utterance pairs despite acoustic contamination. This study tests whether an offline digital-signal-processing (DSP) front end improves a SpeechBrain ECAPA-TDNN encoder on VCTK speech mixed with deterministic composite MUSAN noise [@vctk; @musan; @ecapa; @speechbrain].

**RQ1.** How does composite noise affect verification across 5, 10, 15, and 20 dB test SNR? **RQ2.** Do high-pass, low-pass, and Wiener stages improve the raw-noisy control? **H1.** Full DSP improves F1 and/or EER at low SNR relative to raw-noisy audio.

# DSP methodology

VCTK 0.92 source clips are cropped deterministically, resampled to mono 16 kHz, and mixed with environmental, low-band (20–300 Hz), and high-band (3–7.5 kHz) MUSAN components. At the 16 kHz ECAPA input rate, the observable band ends at the 8 kHz Nyquist frequency. The protocol compares five conditions:

| Condition | Transform after mixing |
|---|---|
| `clean_reference` | Clean 16 kHz reference/ceiling |
| `raw_noisy` | Composite MUSAN noise only |
| `high_pass` | 80 Hz high-pass |
| `high_pass_low_pass` | 80 Hz high-pass + 7.5 kHz low-pass |
| `full_dsp` | Both filters + Wiener filter (window 29) |

The Butterworth filters are zero-phase. Accordingly, this is an offline filtering study, not evidence that the method is deployable in a causal streaming system.

# Models and comparison

The primary model is the pretrained SpeechBrain ECAPA-TDNN speaker encoder [@ecapa; @speechbrain], fine-tuned under the fixed condition/seed protocol. The encoder consumes waveforms rather than handcrafted features. The DSP-only reference uses 40-coefficient MFCC frames over 80 mel bands, summarizes them with coefficient mean and standard deviation, L2-normalizes the result, and scores pairs with cosine similarity. Its results are loaded from saved `evaluation-mfcc-cosine.json` artifacts rather than recomputed here.

```{python}

```

# Experimental controls

The versioned configuration fixes three-second clips, 50 clips per speaker, speaker-disjoint 80/10/10 splits, seeds 11/22/33, and the four test SNRs. All noisy conditions share deterministic source clips, noise provenance, and balanced verification pairs. Thresholds are selected from validation pairs and then fixed on each test protocol; no test-set threshold selection occurs.

The mandated raw-noisy tuning grid spans learning rates {3e-5, 1e-4} and encoder-freeze epochs {0, 1}. The selected values are locked before training every condition and seed.

```{python}
#| label: tuning-results

display(tuning)
```

# Error analysis

False-positive and false-negative cases are retained in each saved evaluation JSON with pair identifiers, score, threshold margin, source identifiers, requested SNR, residual SNR, and MFCC diagnostics. This report intentionally does not regenerate errors or metrics.

```{python}
#| label: error-analysis
error_reports = sorted(STUDY_ROOT.glob("seed-*/*/evaluation-test-snr-*.json"))
if not error_reports:
    raise FileNotFoundError(f"No saved test evaluation reports below {STUDY_ROOT}; run `evaluate`.")
saved_errors = []
for report in error_reports:
    payload = json.loads(report.read_text(encoding="utf-8"))
    saved_errors.extend({**error, "report": str(report.relative_to(PROJECT_ROOT))} for error in payload.get("errors", []))
display(Markdown(f"## Saved error cases ({len(saved_errors)})"))
display(saved_errors[:50])
```

# Limitations

The conclusions apply to VCTK, the deterministic MUSAN construction, the selected ECAPA revision, and this fixed offline protocol. They do not establish robustness to arbitrary microphones, languages, real-time operation, unseen noise distributions, demographic balance, spoofing, or adversarial conditions. The filter chain may remove speaker-relevant detail even when a signal-level diagnostic appears improved.

# Reproducibility

The CLI is the canonical execution layer, `main.ipynb` is a read-only technical dashboard/orchestrator, and this QMD is the final presentation layer. After reviewing and accepting the data licenses, reproduce the complete run with:

```bash
uv sync
uv run python run.py download-data --accept-data-licenses
uv run python run.py --config configs/dsp501-v1.json all
uv run pytest -q
quarto render report.qmd
```

The release bundle excludes raw datasets and records SHA-256 checksums. Verify its contents with `uv run python run.py --config configs/dsp501-v1.json package --dry-run` before packaging.
